messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated tail latency observed for /v1/generate on dedicated pool 'dedicated-east-1'. p95 = 2.6s (SLO 1.0s), p99 = 7.8s. Triggered 2026-02-18T18:15:00Z. Paging: @eng-oncall @ops-sre
alex: oncall (alex) here, looking now.
sophia: seeing a large queue spike — queue_depth = 1200 on pool dedicated-east-1, desired_nodes=6, running=6. Autoscaler queued a scale event but warmup_cooldown prevented immediate add.
liam: streaming stalls reported in traces — clients report stalled chunks mid-stream. likely starvation at worker level (long KV restore).
rachel: adding dashboard links: https://console.redwood/internal/dash/pool/dedicated-east-1?range=15m (watch p95/p99, queue depth, warmup_heatmap)
alex: can we manually scale while autoscaler catches up? I'll trigger manual add +2.
sophia: please also enable overflow routing to a smaller model to shed load if possible. that should reduce per-request GPU cost immediately.
ops-sre: note: node warmup includes KV cache restore (~60-120s depending on snapshot size). autoscaler respects warmup window; that's why autoscale appears delayed.
alex: running: 
```
redwoodctl autoscale set --pool dedicated-east-1 --desired 8 --reason "manual add during latency spike"
```
incident-bot: Action logged: alex requested manual scale -> desired=8.
sophia: manual scale accepted, starting KV prewarm on new nodes. enabling routing: /v1/generate -> model=rw-small-backup for non-critical traffic.
liam: queue_depth now falling from 1200 -> 420 after routing change, but p99 still ~4.2s. streaming stalls still intermittently present (approx 20-30s windows).
rachel: customer impact: support ticket ACME-4321 shows AcmeCorp saw partial streams / stalled responses between 18:15 and 18:24 UTC. marking as potential customer-impacting.
alex: starting KV snapshot restore to new nodes (kick off prewarm job).
sophia: prewarm job started. I'll also bump worker concurrency temporarily (8 -> 12) to increase throughput while warmup finishes. watching memory.
ops-sre: increasing concurrency — keep an eye on OOM / OOM-kill. alert threshold set.
liam: found a set of long-running requests from Acme's batch job (job id: BQ-1234) that pinned GPU for ~40s each — exacerbates tail. can we throttle or redirect long-run background jobs to dedicated burst queue?
sophia: temporarily throttling large-batch submissions by setting route quota via console to protect serving path.
alex: p95 now 1.4s, p99 2.1s — trending the right way.
sophia: KV prewarm finished on 2 new nodes. warmup metrics show KV_hit_rate > 90% on warm nodes.
liam: streaming stalls dropped to nearly zero after KV warmup finished. p95 = 0.98s, p99 = 1.6s. still monitoring.
rachel: drafting customer message: "We experienced degraded streaming responsiveness on dedicated-east-1 from 18:15–18:24 UTC. Root cause: autoscaler warmup + high queue depth due to bursty batch traffic. Mitigation: manual scale, KV prewarm and overflow routing. Impact: partial streaming interruptions for some requests. Follow-up: postmortem and config changes."
ops-sre: proposed follow-ups: 1) reduce autoscaler warmup config (from 180s -> 60s), 2) add burst capacity bucket to allow short-lived oversubscribe, 3) implement faster KV snapshot restore path, 4) add explicit overflow route for heavy background jobs. I'll file RFCs.
alex: quick CLI snippet I ran for manual action: 
```
# manual add
redwoodctl nodes add --pool dedicated-east-1 --count 2 --priority manual
# enable overflow routing
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --overflow-model rw-small-backup
```
sophia: p95 restored under SLO (0.95s), p99 at 1.5s now. marking incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
liam: setting incident severity to sev2 (customer-impacting but contained). creating postmortem ticket: INT-2026-022.
rachel: I'll post customer notification in support and coordinate follow-ups with TAM.
ops-sre: logged action items into RFC board and assigned owners. recommended config change PRs: autoscaler warmup, burst buckets, KV snapshot speedups.
alex: handing off monitoring to @sophia — I'm stepping off in 10m.
sophia: oncall ack. I'll monitor for 30m and escalate if regressions.
incident-bot: RESOLVED: Latency SLOs back within targets at 2026-02-18T18:26:40Z. Final metrics: p95=0.95s, p99=1.5s, queue_depth normalized. Incident duration ~11m. Please update timeline and postmortem.
rachel: thanks team — good quick mitigation. I'll capture timeline and impact and link to postmortem when ready.
ops-sre: follow-ups prioritized. closing slack thread after postmortem created. :lock:
